newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Elec sees chip losses narrowing in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Elec sees chip losses narrowing in 97/98.

text.p: Mitsubishi Electric Corp expects its group loss in the semiconductor sector to narrow in the current business year to end-March 1998, following a bottoming out of 16MB DRAM prices in the second half of fiscal 1996/97, Mitsubishi managing director Masatoshi Umeda told a news conference on Tuesday.
Umeda also said that Mitsubishi Electric forecast a group operating profit of more than 85 billion yen and a parent operating profit of more than 70 billion yen for fiscal 1997/98.
He added that the company aims to post a group operating profit in fiscal 1997/98 in the consumer electronics sector, following a 3.6 billion yen loss in that sector in 1996/97.
Mitsubishi Electric's profit forecasts for fiscal 1997/98 were based on an assumed exchange rate of 115 yen per dollar, he said.

Mitsubishi Electric also said it planned capital expenditure of 220 billion yen in 1997/98, unchanged from the previous year. Of that, investment in the chip division will total 115 billion yen, also unchanged from the prior year.
Asked about the prospects for the company's troubled semiconductor division, Umeda said, "We aim to post a profit (in 1997/98), but it might be very difficult to do so."

He said Mitsubishi Electric posted an operating loss of more than 70 billion yen in the chip division in 1996/97, mainly due to large losses at overseas semiconductor plants, although he did not offer further details.

Umeda said the company is stepping up production of chips other than DRAMs at its U.S. semiconductor plant and recently started integrated production of chips at its German plant. This will raise profitability in the chip division in the current fiscal year, he said.
The company also posted a parent special loss in 1996/97 of five billion yen due to restructuring of its overseas consumer electronics units.
